summary: ZenithAnalytics: duplicate completions during batched ingest triggered autoscaler throttle cascade - post-incident action plan
description:
Issue summary: During a nightly high-throughput batch ingest (10M tokens over 30 minutes) for ZenithAnalytics' dedicated pool in us-east, customers started seeing duplicate completion chunks and a rapid spike in token accounting. This triggered the platform autoscaler to aggressively add/remove nodes which in turn caused rate-limiter thrashing and elevated 5xxs for ~22 minutes.

Impact: Customer reported duplicate completions (some responses duplicated whole 300-token tails), inflated token consumption visible on observer, and temporary elevated latency and 5xx for ~2% of requests. Billing exposure estimated ~+8% token delta for the affected window. Zenith's downstream processors received duplicate payloads, triggering ingestion retries.

Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated), prod | us-east. ZenithAnalytics tenant id: ten-7721.

Steps to reproduce (summary):
1) Synthetic replay of Zenith's batch: 50K requests with 200–400 token completions using the customer's batching mode and prefix cache config.
2) Observe autoscaler triggers when tail latencies exceed 600ms and queued request backlog > 150.
3) Throttles/rate-limiter rules flip to more restrictive policy as nodes cycle and KV cache warms, causing partial replays and duplicated completions in resumed streams.

Observed behavior: Duplicated completion chunks (typically the last 50–100 tokens repeated), autoscaler rapid scale-up followed by scale-down oscillation, rate-limiter returning 429/503 cascades for short windows.

Expected behavior: Single, ordered completion per request. Smooth autoscaling with gradual capacity adjustments and stable rate limit enforcement.

Logs / artifacts: System traces attached to confluence page. Key traces show repeated request replays from gateway: request-id trace links in Confluence. Kernel selection logs show quantized kernel used for half the instances during window. KV-cache hit-rate dropped to 12% initially then recovered.
comments: 2026-03-12 02:18 - Maya Chen (Support): Ticket opened after ZenithSupport alerted via #support-escalations. Immediate mitigation requested and customer notified that engineering was triaging.

2026-03-12 02:25 - Rafael Ortega (SRE): Confirmed duplicate chunk pattern from traces (request replay observed when stream resumed after transient 503). Suspected interplay between autoscaler/node recycle and our prefix/KV cache warming logic.

2026-03-12 03:05 - ZenithAnalytics (Customer): Confirmed duplicates are causing downstream ingestion to drop records. Asked for immediate temporary throttle reduction and refund window for affected tokens.

2026-03-12 04:10 - Rafael Ortega (SRE): Applied temporary autoscaler cooldown (increase scale-down window to 10m) and enabled conservative rate-limiter policy for Zen pool. Duplicates and 5xxs subsided; monitoring green by 04:35.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: duplication correlated with stream resume after short-lived 503s; repeated writes from gateway session replay logic observed in traces.
Hypothesis 1: Gateway replay + resumed streaming interactions caused the serving-runtime to replay the last completion fragment due to missing idempotency checks on reattach.
Hypothesis 2: Rapid autoscaler churn caused inconsistent kernel selection and KV-cache warmup regressions leading to transient stream resets and gateway replay attempts.

Telemetry: KV cache hit-rate dropped to 12% at incident start, steady at ~85% after stabilizing. Autoscaler metrics: 6 scale events in a 9-minute window. Rate-limiter logs show policy flips from 'moderate' to 'restrictive' twice during the window.

Root cause (conclusion): Combination of (A) gateway-level request replay on perceived transient 503s during stream resumption and (B) aggressive autoscaler scale-down policy that enabled node churn before KV caches warmed, which together created a replay loop producing duplicate completion fragments.

Contributing factor: A recent change to the autoscaler aggressiveness feature flag (ASG-aggressive=true) rolled out to dedicated pools for cost optimization two days earlier; the Zen pool hit the new threshold under batch load.
Evidence links: Traces and histogram dashboards posted to Confluence page; kernel-selection and autoscaler event timelines captured there.
resolution_notes: Immediate mitigation (2026-03-12 03:50): Increased autoscaler scale-down grace period to 10m for Zenith's pool; disabled 'ASG-aggressive' for the pool; applied conservative rate-limiter fallback rules to prevent replay amplification.

Code fix (2026-03-13): Backported a patch to gateway reattach logic to enforce idempotent stream re-entry: server now uses resume-token validation and discards duplicate completion chunks when sequence numbers overlap. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2291.
Config change (2026-03-13): Updated default dedicated-pool autoscaler profile to use smoother ramp (min step 10% / max step 40%) and KV cache pre-warm hook when scale events exceed threshold.
Customer remediation: Issued a billing credit for the affected window equivalent to estimated +8% token delta; customer notified and accepted the credit (credit applied on 2026-03-14 invoice).

Monitoring: Added alert 'dedicated.pool.duplicate-completion-rate' and dashboard tile for autoscaler-churn-rate; synthetic test added to nightly suite to replay Zenith-style batch and detect duplicates within 5 minutes of deploy.
Status: Fix deployed to prod for dedicated pools in us-east on 2026-03-13 22:10. Verified with customer-run replay and production telemetry.
follow_up_actions: 1) Postmortem writeup to be published to Confluence by 2026-03-16 (owner: Rafael Ortega).
2) Rollout plan to remove 'ASG-aggressive' flag globally only after 2-week canary and additional load tests (owner: Platform Team).
3) Add resume-token idempotency unit/integration tests and include in CI gating for gateway (owner: Gateway Team, due 2026-03-20).
4) Review billing exposure calculation for batched workloads; create automated token-delta check that flags unusual deltas per tenant (owner: Billing, due 2026-03-24).
5) Schedule a customer-facing review session with ZenithAnalytics to go over root cause and safeguards (owner: Customer Success, scheduled 2026-03-18).
